content.title: Interesting idea, but a bit over-claimed. Detailed experiments are required to validate the contributions.
content.review:
Summary: This paper proposes a two-stream network to tackle the single-view depth estimation problem. One stream predicts disparity map directly from the input image, while the other stream synthesizes a novel view image and then estimates the disparity via stereo matching algorithms. The outputs of the two streams are then fused together according to the estimated confidence maps, to generate the final result.


Strength:
+ The idea of synthesizing another view and then do stereo matching seems interesting and novel 
+ The proposed method achieves good performance on the KITTI benchmark
+ The proposed method seems to transfer well to other driving scene data quite well visually


Weakness:
- In the introduction, the authors list three key contributions. However, the authors cannot really say they “propose” a self-supervised method for disparity prediction. The actual contribution is the improved disparity consistency loss (Eqn 3). However, no experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of this loss.
- More details are required for the last paragraph of Section 3.2. In addition to SGBM, how do the authors incorporate ELAS and the Bayesian inference strategy?
- In Section 3.3, the authors claim “confidence maps are trained separately in a self-supervised fashion without using ground truth depth labels”. However, how exactly the authors train this network remains unclear to me.
- The text in Section 3.4 seems messy. Also, “end-to-end” usually indicates training the whole system in one stage. I feel that the authors should not use this term here.
- Table 1 is a bit confusing. I am not sure what “stereo only” is and what “mono only” is. Are they actually the two streams of the whole system? The improvement over Ferrera et al. seems quite marginal (3.03% v.s. 3.01%). My concern is whether the improvement is only on the KITTI dataset or generalizable.
- In the first paragraph of Section 4.2, the authors say that they use post-processing to eliminate the effect of dis-occlusions. However, I did not find relevant descriptions in Table 2 and the corresponding description. So I assume “Our full” uses this post-processing. It is necessary to show the raw performance without post-processing. Also, I wonder if the authors can show the performance of the stereo-matching stream (w/ and w/o post-processing). Another interesting study will be, replacing the synthesized image with the ground truth right-view image, so that we can know the upper bound performance of this idea. This might be more informative than Table 3.
- Comparing to some of the methods in Table 2 that use only a single-view during training, the proposed method uses stereo pairs. It is better to mention this in the table.
- I wonder if the proposed method can only work well on the driving scene. To test the generalizability, previous approaches test their method on other depth estimation dataset (e.g., Make3D) without fine-tuning. Maybe the authors can also show such a study.  


Other comments:
* Why use the term “spectral consistency”? “Photometric consistency” or “appearance consistency” seems to be more commonly used by the community.
* The images in Figure 3 are not spatially aligned.
* I am a bit not sure the purpose of Figure 7.


---- Post-rebuttal comments----

Thanks for the response. However, the rebuttal does not fully address my concerns. The current presentation is not good enough, and the technical contribution seems limited (very likely due to the presentation). Thus, I keep my initial score.

I encourage the authors to re-write the paper and submit it to the next venue. In particular, the authors should use (ablation) experiments to support/validate the proposed technical novelty.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 4: The reviewer is confident but not absolutely certain that the evaluation is correct

content.title: Feedback for review comments
content.comment:
Thank you for the detailed suggestions.
1. Thanks for pointing out this. We have changed this contribution ‘propose a self-supervised method’ to ‘improve a self-supervised method’, and add an additional experiment to verify the effectiveness of this in Table 1 in the updated paper.

2. Semi-global matching usually takes a longer time as they need to do global optimization to the cost function across the entire image (but slightly more accurate), ELAS matching uses some reliable ‘supported points’ from sobel features for matching instead of the entire image, thus reduce the searching burden and time. We incorporate these two together, to add cost optimization from SGBM only on the reliable “supported points” instead of on the entire image to leverage both of their performance but reduce the computation and time.

3. The network of confidence map generation is described as follows: provided a disparity map from either single image stereo algorithm or single image depth estimation network, we will assign a group of label points (20 in our implementation) in the range of [0, 1] (0 means wrong and 1 means correct) based on the evaluation metrics we selected for two different methods. After training the entire images with the defined labels as supervision as a classification problem, only the higher confidence score for each pixel in each method will be selected for fusion. This strategy is conducted currently in an unsupervised way, it can also be trained with ground truth labels to provide even more reliable confidence if needed.

4. Thanks for your suggestion. We will remove this wording in the updated paper. 

5. Yes, the “stereo only” and “mono only” in Table 1 represent the single image stereo based on view synthesis and spectral consistency based single image depth estimation, respectively. The reason for the slight improvement on [Ferrera et al.] is that [Ferrera et al.] relies on the ground truth disparity information when training their data-based branch, while our method does not use ground truth for training.

6. Thank you for our suggested experiments on the post-processing procedure based on consistency check. We add an additional experiment in Table 1 to show the effectiveness of this post-processing operation. An additional study to replace the synthesized image with the ground truth right-view image is also added in Table 3 in the updated paper.

7. Thank you for your advice. In the caption of Table 2, we point out the exact image type used for training. We highlight that the first three methods [Eigen… to DeepCRF] are using single-view image only based on supervised training, the middle five methods [SfMLearner…to CC Ranjan] are using monocular image sequences, and the last ones [Garg… to ours] are using stereo image pair for training. But for testing, all these methods, except [Pilzer & et al. Unsup-depthGAN, 2018] that uses stereo images, only utilize single-view image.


8. It is possible that for normal scenes the trained model is not able to generalize very well. In our trial, the single image depth estimation method is able to generate reasonable output for normal scenes. However, without training, the view synthesis network will not work well on those scenes, resulting in an unsatisfactory stereo matching output. In this case, the fusion output will get hurt instead.

9. Thanks for point out this. Our motivation to use “spectral consistency” is to distinguish from the spatial consistency (position consistency) and temporal consistency (cross sequences). We will make it clear that it is the same concept of photometric consistency or appearance consistency.

10 . We will correct alignment issue in Fig. 3. 

11. The point cloud in Fig. 7 is mainly to show the real 3D effect in addition to depth map, as point cloud is more straightforward for people to observe the 3D scenes.

content.title: Review for "Single Image Depth Estimation Based on Spectral Consistency and Predicted View"
content.review:
### Summary
This paper proposes a self-supervised framework to tackle single view depth estimation problem.
Different from previous methods that directly estimate depth map from a single image, this paper proposes a depth fusion method which fuse depth estimations from (1) single-view (2) stereo matching of a synthesized stereo pair.
Specifically, 
(1) a disparity network is trained to estimate both left and right disparity maps.
(2) a view synthesis network is trained to synthesize left/right view from a given view. Then SGBM is applied on the synthesized pair to estimate the disparity map.
(3) To fuse the disparity estimations from (1) and (2), a confidence network is trained to predict the confidence for each prediction. (4) Finally, a winner takes all appraoch is adopted to select depth prediction from (1) or (2).
To train the networks,
(1) single view depth estimation network is trained in a self-supervised manner, i.e. photometric-based loss (spectral consistency loss) as the main supervisional loss
(2) GAN-based loss is used to train the view synthesis network
(3) To train the confidence network, conventional confidence measures are used as the label.

### Strength
#### interesting idea of combining single-view depth and single-view stereo estimation
Personally, I like the idea of single-view stereo estimation though sometimes I think that it is a little bit "unrealistic" (no offence). However, if we can do single view depth estimation, why not single view stereo estimation.
Moreover, I believe stereo matching should produce more accurate depth estimation than single view depth estimation, though depending on the quality of the synthesized image.

#### higher accuracy when compared to single-view depth estimation frameworks
In Table 2, the authors have shown better performance when compared to prior arts. However, I believe the comparison is based on the "without ImageNet pretrained" setup. This work has shown better performance than the popular monodepth2 framework under this setup. It will be more convincing if the authors can show better performance in the "with ImageNet pretrained" setup thus it will be the real STOA result.

### Weakness
#### Overclaiming of contribution
The authors have stated three contributions, including introduce a self-supervised method based on the spectral consistency for image consistency.
However, the only difference I can see is extending the left-right consistency [proposed by monodepth] by a robust loss, i.e. BerHu loss.
This doesn't create a significant contribution, especially under the circumstance that no experiment support.

#### incomplete diagram illustration
In figure.1 (Inference), the diagram over simplifies the inference process. e.g. the view synthesis network doesn't output a depth map directly but the network+SGBM outputs the depth map. Also, if I understand correctly, the confidence network is missed for the fusion as well.

#### unconvincing qualitative result / depth fusion scheme
Though the authors have shown improvement on quantative result using the proposed method (with stereo fusion), the qualitative result looks worse than my expectation.
i.e. from Figure 3, the output from single image stereo shows artefact on ground (textureless regions). In row 1, the artifect are passed to the full output after fusion. In row 2, the artefect are not passed to the full output in contrast. The confidence prediction/fusion scheme looks a little bit random.
Could authors shed some lights on the fusion scheme? e.g. what scenes will it be useful/fail?

#### writing issue
I would suggest the authors proofread before submission. There are some writings/sentences are not clear to me / typo.
e.g.1 Sec 4.2 (para. 2): 
For the predicted view-based single image stereo network, We train the IT from scratch ...
- We-->we
- train the "IT": what does it mean?

e.g.2 Sec 3.4 
These two networks can be combined for joint training once being trained to obtain the ability
of geometric reasoning for the task of view synthesis and stereo matching separately. End-to-end
training of the whole pipeline can These two networks can be combined for joint training once being
trained to obtain the ability of geometric.
- incomplete sentence
- repeated sentence

These low-level writing issues give an impression that the article is written in a rush and lower confidence on the paper quality.

### Conclusion
Given the insufficient experimental support and explanation, I will give rejection at this stage.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 5: The reviewer is absolutely certain that the evaluation is correct and very familiar with the relevant literature

content.title: Feedback for review comments
content.comment:
1.	Thank you for asking. In addition to the pointed contribution, there are another two major contributions, which are stereo reconstruction based on a single image, which had to be stereo images previously, and the fusion of two different depth estimation methods using the same single image, which enjoys the benefits of both methods.

2.	Thanks for the advice. We drew the inference part of Fig. 1 in a simplified way, which is mainly to introduce the brief structure for readers to grasp the basic idea. We will add more details in the figure in the final version. 


3.	The main reason for this is on the crosswalks. As the training scenes are mainly normal roads without crosswalks, when testing images appear with crosswalks, the confidence map from spectral consistency may be lower than that of stereo matching as crosswalks are unseen in training, for which it accepts stereo matching disparities with slightly rough road surface. That could be the reason why our fusion method mostly can prevent serious rough surface and over-smooth issues, but exists artifacts on crosswalks. More examples on common scenes are added in the updated paper, to show the effectiveness of our fusion method.

4.	Thanks for your detailed suggestion. It’s a typo at the place “train the IT”, which should be “train it”. We modified those low-level writing issues in the updated paper.

content.title: Review for single image depth estimation based on spectral consistency and predicted view
content.review:
This paper deals with an important problem in computer vision of generating depth estimates from a simgle input image. Banking on the fact that single image depth estimation is usually inferior to depth estimation from stereo, the authors propose a novel architecture to infer accurate disparity by leveraging both spectral-consistency based learning model and view-prediction based stereo reconstruction algorithm.

The first part where the authors build the spectral consistency based depth estimation seems to be entirely similar to the development mentioned in [Godard et al. 2017]. The L_{cs} term just checks for the upper bound of the disparity in addition to the flow mentioned in the reference paper.

The single image stereo by predicted view is mostly the Cycle-GAN [Zhu et al. 2017] formulation with no new novelty in it.

Finally, the fusion algorithm to generate the combined disparity map seems to be mostly from [Tosi et al 2017] paper.

The technical contribution of this work is quite limited as it just computes the outputs for two established methods and then proposed to use another paper to fuse / conditionally select one of the outputs from the disparity generation methods.

The results reported seem to support the idea that the combination of two strong methods with a nonlinear combination algorithm beats each one of them individually. The novelty of this method remains a major bottleneck for this paper.

For this venue, I would go with a reject decision since this work does not propose anything to further the research field in this domain.

content.title: Feedback for review comments
content.comment:
Thank you for the comment.

(1) Though the view synthesis process in single image stereo adopts the basic idea from Cycle-GAN, we extend it to multi-scale generators and discriminators to extract both holistic and local features. The integration of novel view synthesis into a stereo matching algorithm that combines both SGBM and ELAS enables it possible to incorporate the benefit from stereo matching algorithm from single image only, which is a contribution. The usage of Cycle-GAN makes the stereo reconstruction based on a single image to be applicable, which had to be stereo images previously. 

(2) The main target in [Tosi et al., 2017] is to train confidence measures on classic stereo algorithms. We extend the similar idea to adaptively select confidence from both predicted view-based single image stereo method and spectral- consistency based disparity prediction methods. This extension directly enhances the performance of single image depth estimation.

(3) The largest contribution of the work is that we contribute a new method for disparity estimation from a single image. By observing the fact that stereo matching based algorithms are able to generate clear object boundary but usually results in wrong matchings on low-texture regions like the ground, and single image depth estimation algorithms often generate smoother output, but bring ambiguity inferences and blurred object boundary due to missing perspectives, we propose a new method to leverage the benefits simultaneously from these two. After training, given one image as input, our method will act as a new method in the real application, to produce disparities enjoying both clear boundary and least wrong correspondences. The improvement on both methods and the proposed idea of merging these methods with confidence to compensate each other noticeably increase the depth estimation effect based on a single image.
